title: Contract renewals desk

contract.description: One agreement approaching its end date: the record the desk exists to decide about. Enters the window as its endDate approaches, and every one of them is looked at — the window is worked down to zero every week, so a contract is never searched for, only reached in order.

actions.constraint: every contract in the window is looked at — nothing is skipped and nothing is searched for; ordering by endDate is how the team decides what to handle first
only from status awaiting-review, applied in place on the row
only from status awaiting-review, applied in place on the row; a decision, not a deletion — the contract keeps its record

vocabularies.status: three fixed values (awaiting-review | renewal-sent | lapsing) — where a contract stands, not a thing with a life of its own. Becomes richer the day the renewal itself gets tracked (sent, countersigned, filed), which would be a new object, not more stops on this field.
vocabularies.accountManager: a name carried on the contract so the specialist knows who to talk to. Fails the litmus test: no screen shows a manager, nothing edits one. Reopens if the desk ever assigns contracts to managers or views a manager's book.
vocabularies.counterparty: the company name as text on the contract. Reopens the day contracts are read grouped by company or a company gets a detail screen of its own.

openQuestions: Where the stream comes from: which system feeds the window, and how wide the window is (how many days before endDate a contract enters) — the feed's decision, inherited here as given data.
What happens downstream of renewal-sent: who picks the renewal up, and whether that handoff ever needs a screen on this desk.

Whether a decided contract leaves the window at once or stays visible with its status until the week rolls — built as staying visible, so the week's record is on screen; the first week of real use decides.
